description:
pkix-lint/src/deviation.rs

Deviation is a pub struct with all-pub fields and no constructor. The
validation (non-empty justification, non-empty authorized_by) lives in
DeviationStore::add at line 667-674:

    pub fn add(&mut self, mut deviation: Deviation) -> Result<(), DeviationAddError> {
        if deviation.justification.is_empty() {
            return Err(DeviationAddError::EmptyField(\"justification\".into()));
        }
        if deviation.authorized_by.is_empty() {
            return Err(DeviationAddError::EmptyField(\"authorized_by\".into()));
        }
        ...
        // Normalize the issuer-dn-contains substring to lowercase
        if deviation.scope.kind == SCOPE_KIND_ISSUER_DN_CONTAINS {
            ...
        }
    }

This means a Deviation constructed via struct literal:

    let d = Deviation {
        id: \"x\".into(),
        target_lint: \"foo\".into(),
        scope: DeviationScope::issuer_dn_contains(\"ACME CORP\"),
        ...
        justification: \"\".into(),       // ← empty, would be rejected by add
        authorized_by: \"\".into(),       // ← empty, would be rejected by add
        ...
    };

is *constructable but useless*. The validation never runs. And then:

    d.scope.matches(cert)  // works — scope is matched
    d.applies_to(cert, now)  // works — but doesn't check
                             //   justification/authorized_by

So a caller can use a Deviation directly (e.g., pass it to
DeviationScope::matches) and bypass the validation entirely.

# What goes wrong for the caller

1. *Implicit dependency on the add path.* The struct literal looks
   like it should work, doc comments describe it, but unless the
   caller routes through DeviationStore::add, the invariants are
   uncomputed.

2. *Issuer-DN-contains case folding.* The add() method lowercase-
   normalizes the substring. A Deviation constructed directly with
   `DeviationScope::issuer_dn_contains(\"ACME CORP\")` and then matched
   without going through add() will silently fail to match (because
   matches() compares against pre-lowercased substring per the
   constructor's own contract).

3. *Builder construction.* OSCAL parse creates Deviation values then
   pushes them to add(). That's correct. But a caller who reads
   deviations from their own source (TOML, YAML, a database) and
   constructs Deviation literals directly bypasses all validation.

# The right shape

Either:

  (a) Provide Deviation::new(...) -> Result<Deviation, EmptyField>
      that does the validation and field-normalization at
      construction time. Make the fields pub(crate) so direct
      struct-literal construction outside the crate is not
      allowed. DeviationStore::add then becomes a duplicate-check.

  (b) A typestate builder: DeviationBuilder::new(id, target_lint,
      scope).justification(...).authorized_by(...).build()
      with the builder enforcing required fields at compile time.

  (c) #[non_exhaustive] on Deviation forces callers through some
      constructor (struct literals fail to compile outside the
      crate). Pair that with Deviation::new(...) for the
      constructor.

# Forward fit

Pre-1.0 fix. Closes both this and PKIX-hy2e.22 partially (the
#[non_exhaustive] line of attack). The two together produce a
properly validated, evolvable Deviation type.
title: API contract: Deviation construction-vs-validation split forces every caller to use DeviationStore::add
